text:
Zara: Offsite checklist question: who has experience flying with a guitar? Thinking of bringing my travel-sized acoustic to Prague. Any tips for cabin/checked, case recommendations, or how to avoid damage?

Marcus: I flew with a small uke and it survived in the cabin under the seat. For a travel guitar, try to gate-check if the airline allows it as a carry-on. Soft gig bag + extra bubble wrap around the headstock.

Leah: If it's a full-size acoustic, you might need to check it. Get a hard case if you check. Put a shirt or foam around the neck to prevent movement. Also take pics of it before travel.

tripbot: airline-policy-check: most carriers allow one carry-on + personal item. Musical instruments may be carried on if they fit in the overhead bin or under seat; gate-checking is common. Check size limits and fees with your carrier.

Noah: If you can, buy a seat for the instrument. Expensive but guaranteed space. Otherwise, buy insurance or an instrument protection add-on.

Zara: Good ideas. Poll: reply "carry-on" if you think try cabin, "check" if too risky, or "buy-seat" for seat buy. Also any recommended gig bag brands?

Marcus: Gator and SKB make solid cases. If budget is tight, get a thick padded case and tape a fragile sticker.

Leah: Also remember to bring a capo and a small string kit in carry-on. You'll be sad if you break a string mid-offsite.
